locator.text: Equation (5.20), p. 53, in the proof of Lemma 5.2

evidence: paper: \int_0^\infty r\,u_{z,n}\,dr = q^{1-A+\lambda_n}\int_0^\infty R\,U_n\,dR,\qquad \int_0^\infty r\Bigl(\sum_{i+j=n} u_{z,i}u_{z,j} + p_n\Bigr)dr = q^{1-2A+\lambda_n}\int_0^\infty R\Bigl(\sum_{i+j=n} U_iU_j + \Pi_n\Bigr)dR

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean never forms the two physical-variable integrals of (5.20) and states no q^{1-A+λ_n} / q^{1-2A+λ_n} conversion. It works throughout in the inner radius R: the two inner right-hand sides are rows 0 and 4 of `PositiveOrderMoments.rowDensity` (row 4 carries −(R²/2)∂_RΠ_n, i.e. ∫RΠ_n already replaced by the integration by parts of eq-p053-5), and the conclusion the paper draws from (5.20) — that both integrals vanish — is stated directly in inner form by `repaired_moment_data`: moment B 1 (u n) = 0 and moment B 1 (conv n u u + pressureHistory) = 0, over [0,B] rather than (0,∞). The only physical↔inner radial rescaling lemma found anywhere in the repository is `RenormalizedHeatMoment.integral_weighted_radial_scale` (line 643), ∫_{r>0} r²(q^b g(r/√q)) dr = q^{b+3/2}∫_{R>0} R² g(R) dR, which carries the weight r² of the angular moment displayed above (5.19), not the weight r of (5.20); no weight-r analogue was found. Severity low: the subsequent Lean development (the integral balances and the stress support of Lemma 5.2) uses only the inner-variable vanishing, so nothing downstream needs the physical form.
